[[ ## thread ## ]]
From: Frank Osei
To: Desmond Ortiz
Subject: Job 2142 – why we lost money

Desmond,

Job 2142 closed 18% under margin. That's not a blip, that's a leak.

I need the breakdown by Friday: labor, materials, change orders, anything you billed late. If it was a bid mistake, say so. If it was site mismanagement, name it.

We can't keep eating these. Get me the numbers and your take on what we do different next time.

Frank

---

From: Desmond Ortiz
To: Frank Osei
Subject: Job 2142 – margin breakdown and drivers

Frank,

Got it. I ran the numbers this morning, and here's what Job 2142 actually cost us.

**Labor** — the biggest leak. We came in about 9% over estimate on field hours. Crew stayed on site an extra week waiting on the steel delivery, and that idle time wasn't reallocated. I've flagged the specific dates and crews in the workpaper.

**Materials** — about 4% over. Two line items (rebar and fasteners) spiked after the bid was locked, and we didn't have escalation clauses in the sub contracts. That's on us for not pushing back when the vendor revised.

**Change orders** — here's where I think we left money on the table. We had three approved change orders, but only one got billed within the month. The other two — one for site prep, one for the drainage adjustment — sat in the field for three weeks before we invoiced. That's roughly 3% of the margin swing right there, not because the work wasn't done, but because we billed late.

**Bid itself** — I'll be straight: the original estimate was thin on labor. We assumed a 2% contingency, but given the crew mix we actually fielded, it should've been 5%. That's a bid mistake, and I'd rather own it now than pretend otherwise.

**What I'd do different next time:**
1. Build labor idle time into the bid — or at minimum, have a clause that covers weather/delivery delays.
2. Invoice change orders the week they're approved, not when the field crew remembers. I'll set a 48-hour rule on our next job.
3. Review the labor estimate against the actual crew mix before we submit. I can add that as a checklist item for the estimators.

Happy to walk you through the full breakdown if you want — I can block time Thursday afternoon.

Des

---

From: Frank Osei
To: Desmond Ortiz
Subject: Re: Job 2142 – margin breakdown and drivers

Des,

Good breakdown. Numbers make sense. The change order billing is the easiest fix—48-hour rule, make it stick. Labor idle is the bigger one; we can't eat that again. I want the escalation clause reviewed on all subs going forward.

Thursday works. Block 2pm. Bring the workpaper and the bid sheet. We'll go line by line.

Frank
